Branson describes their early song titles as unimaginative.
The Interviewer learns Branson writes the music, and Preston does not read music.
The Interviewer asks why they chose to play nylon-string guitars.
Branson explains his father’s musical background influenced him, and how he started with quiet, rhythm-less playing.
Branson describes how his uncle and father’s brother introduced him to the nylon-string guitar.
Branson talks about his sister sending him a CD of Rodrigo y Gabriela, inspiring him to explore different elements in his music.
Preston talks about how he started playing electric guitar and got into classic rock and flamenco.
Preston explains how Branson taught him to play nylon-string guitar.
Branson discusses his drumming background and how he started at age six.
Branson reveals he was not good at reading music, which influenced his decision to move away from marching band.

youtube_description:
This video is from our meeting with ASCAP on Feb 12, 2010. 

In celebration of music from all over the world, the Taalbi Brothers bring NYC street percussion, spirited gypsy beats, wild chord changes fueled by classical music, and powerful melodies honoring legends of the guitar.

The Taalbi Brothers story begins with long winters in the basement of their midwest home... 
(story continues at http://www.taalbibrothers.com)

Buy the album "Ameksa" on iTunes: http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/ameksa-ep/id467833905

For more information on the Taalbi Brothers, please visit http://www.taalbibrothers.com or you can email us at taalbibrothers@gmail.com
